harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1's password policy via a pwquality.conf.d drop-in (minlen=12, minclass=3), confirmed it's wired into PAM (system-auth/password-auth already require pam_pwquality.so), validated enforcement end-to-end with real passwd attempts by an actual (non-root) user both before and after a full node reboot, and confirmed the boot identity changed to prove the restart was genuine.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 10): libpwquality installed, pam_pwquality.so already required in /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth
Created /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/90-complexity.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3; confirmed base pwquality.conf was left unmodified with no duplicate settings
Used pwscore to confirm short/low-class passwords are rejected and a 12+ char, 3-class password is accepted

Created a real test user (complextest), set an initial password via chpasswd, then as that non-root user attempted a weak passwd change (rejected, exit 10) and a compliant one (accepted, exit 0); cleaned up the user
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, policy file contents, PAM wiring
Issued a backgrounded reboot on node1 so the tool call could acknowledge before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned, confirming boot_id changed from aad96cc9-79e8-42b7-a522-ebc71e3a96c3 to 261923fb-c879-41b2-bfca-0dcf76de5448
Re-verified policy file contents and PAM wiring persisted after reboot
Repeated the real-user passwd enforcement test post-restart with a new test user (posttest): weak password rejected (exit 10), compliant password accepted (exit 0); cleaned up the user

evidence.requirement: Password policy requires min 12 characters, min 3 character classes, applied via PAM on node1
evidence.summary: Confirmed pam_pwquality.so already required by system-auth/password-auth, and installed minlen=12/minclass=3 via a clean drop-in with no conflicting duplicate entries in the base file

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced for real password changes (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: pwscore rejected weak/low-class passwords and accepted a compliant one; a real non-root user (complextest) had a weak passwd change rejected (exit 10) and a compliant one accepted (exit 0); test user cleaned up
Captured boot_id (aad96cc9-79e8-42b7-a522-ebc71e3a96c3), uptime, and confirmed policy file and PAM wiring present before reboot
Backgrounded reboot command returned its 'scheduled' acknowledgement immediately, before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node actually restarted (changed boot identity), not just delayed
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) during reboot, then came back with boot_id 261923fb-c879-41b2-bfca-0dcf76de5448, different from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: policy config and enforcement still active
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check confirmed policy file and PAM wiring persisted; a fresh real user (posttest) had a weak passwd change rejected (exit 10) and a compliant one accepted (exit 0), then was cleaned up
